mainTopic: עירובין 17b — The army-camp leniencies (burial, hand-washing, דמאי, עירוב), and the opening משנה on boards around wells
overview: This עמוד finishes the משנה's list of leniencies for an army camp and then opens a new פרק. First the גמרא explains that a soldier is buried where he fell even when he has people to bury him, so he is not a מת מצוה. רב ביבי then defends the rule that a מת מצוה is buried in its place: the ברייתא that lets a corpse be moved deals only with one lying on a boundary path. Next, אביי limits the camp's exemption from hand-washing to washing before the meal. Washing after the meal stays required because of dangerous מלח סדומית. The גמרא grounds the camp's דמאי leniency in בית הלל's ruling. It then limits the עירוב exemption to עירובי חצירות, since walking past the תחום may carry Torah lashes. רבי יונתן and רב אחא בר יעקב argue whether that לאו can carry מלקות, and רב אשי notes that the verse says 'go out,' not 'carry out.' After the הדרן, the second פרק opens with a משנה about boards (פסין) set up around wells: how many, how big, how far apart, and how close to the well, continuing on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The army rule covers a corpse that has people to bury it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the rule 'a soldier is buried where he fell' applies even when he has relatives or friends who could bury him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The rule is needed for a case] where he has people to bury him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its earlier question about why the army rule was needed. The answer is that the rule applies even to a dead soldier who has people available to bury him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא asked: a corpse found with no one to care for it is a מת מצוה, and a מת מצוה is buried where it lies anyway, so why teach this? The answer is that the army rule goes further. In an army camp, even a soldier who is not a מת מצוה is buried on the spot.

keyTerms.meaning: people who will bury him (relatives, friends, community)
that he has
the place where he was killed is where he is buried (the army-camp rule under discussion)

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a sentence. It answers a question earlier: why the army rule is needed if a מת מצוה is buried in place anyway.

phrases.english: [It is needed for a case] where he has people to bury him,
phrases.notes: Answers the earlier question of why the army rule is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question (on the previous amud) of why the army rule is needed if a מת מצוה is buried in place anyway.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The army rule teaches that a fallen soldier is buried on the spot even when he has people to bury him, meaning even when he is not a מת מצוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines what counts as a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a מת מצוה is only a corpse with no one to bury it. If calling out would bring people to answer, it is not a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Which is a מת מצוה? Any corpse that has no one to bury it. If someone calls out and others answer him, this is not a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that a corpse with available buriers is not a מת מצוה. This supports the answer in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets two signs that a corpse is not a מת מצוה: it has people to bury it, or people are close enough to answer a call for help. This proves that the soldier in step 1 is not a מת מצוה. So the army rule really is teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: an abandoned corpse with no one to bury it; anyone who finds it must bury it
which is? (a defining question)
one calls out and others answer, meaning help is within reach

steps.whatToRemember: A מת מצוה is only a corpse that truly has no one else to bury it. Once help is available, it loses that status.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Which is a met מצוה?
Any [corpse] that has no one to bury it.
If one calls out and others answer him —
this is not a met מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source showing that a corpse with available buriers is not a מת מצוה, which backs up step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a soldier with people to bury him falls outside the category of מת מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא defining מת מצוה as a corpse with no one to bury it, or one where calling out would bring no answer.

steps.title: Does a מת מצוה really stay where it is found?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that a מת מצוה is buried in its place. A ברייתא says a corpse found on a road is moved to the side of the road, or into a less valuable field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a מת מצוה really acquire its place? But it was taught: One who finds a corpse lying on a main road moves it to the right or left of the road. If the choice is an uncultivated field or a plowed field, he moves it to the uncultivated field. If the choice is a plowed field or a sown field, he moves it to the plowed field. If both are plowed, both are sown, or both are uncultivated, he moves it to any side he wishes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the basic rule behind steps 1 and 2: that a מת מצוה is buried exactly where it lies. It quotes a ברייתא that clearly allows moving such a corpse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole discussion assumed that a מת מצוה 'acquires its place,' meaning it is buried on the spot. This ברייתא lets the finder move it off the road and into the least damaging field. When the fields are equal, he may move it in any direction at all, which seems to contradict that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: acquires its place: it is buried where it is found
a main public road (from Latin strata)
an uncultivated, unworked field
a plowed field, prepared but not yet sown
a sown field with seed in it

steps.confusionAlert: The fields are ranked by how much harm a grave would cause. An uncultivated field loses the least, a plowed field more, and a sown field the most. The corpse goes to the least damaging option.

phrases.english: And does a met מצוה acquire its place?
But wasn't it taught: One who finds a corpse lying on a main road —
moves it to the right of the road
or to the left of the road.
An uncultivated field and a plowed field —
he moves it to the uncultivated field.
A plowed field and a sown field —
he moves it to the plowed field.
If both were plowed,
both sown, or both uncultivated —
he moves it to any direction he wishes!
phrases.notes: This is the strongest part of the challenge: the corpse may be moved anywhere at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining מת מצוה to challenging the rule that a מת מצוה is buried in its place.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumed rule that a מת מצוה acquires its place (מת מצוה קנה מקומו).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows moving a found corpse off the road and into fields, even in any direction when the fields are equal. That suggests a מת מצוה does not have to be buried where it lies.

steps.title: רב ביבי: the corpse was lying on a boundary strip
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי explains that the ברייתא deals with a corpse on a מיצר, a boundary path. Since moving it off the strip is already permitted, it may be moved in any direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said: Here we are dealing with a corpse lying on a boundary strip. Since permission was given to move it off the boundary strip, he may move it to any direction he wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי answers the challenge. The ברייתא is about a special case, a corpse lying on a boundary path that people need to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a מת מצוה stays where it is found. A corpse lying on a public boundary path would block the way and cause harm, so it must be moved anyway. Once moving it is already allowed, it may go in any direction, so the ברייתא is an exception and the basic rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: here we are dealing with... (narrows a source to a specific case)
a boundary strip or narrow path between fields, used for passage
since (once one thing is permitted, a further step follows)
permission was given

steps.whatToRemember: A מת מצוה is buried where it is found. The ברייתא about moving a corpse covers only a corpse on a boundary path, which had to be moved anyway. Once moving it is allowed, any direction is fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the rule that a מת מצוה acquires its place. It also shows the reasoning of מתוך: once an exception permits one step, the further details follow from it.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּמֵת מוּטָּל עַל הַמֵּיצַר עָסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a corpse lying on the boundary strip.
Since permission was given
to move it from the boundary strip —
he moves it to any direction he wishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי: הָכָא בְּמֵת מוּטָּל עַל הַמֵּיצַר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from step 3 by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא refers only to a corpse lying on a boundary path.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that any מת מצוה may be moved wherever the finder wants, so it does not acquire its place.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מת מצוה does acquire its place. Only when it lies on a boundary path, where it must be moved anyway, may it be moved in any direction.

steps.title: Soldiers are exempt only from washing before the meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next exemption in the משנה, freedom from washing hands. אביי limits it to מים ראשונים and says מים אחרונים remain a חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said soldiers are exempt from washing hands. אביי said: this was taught only about the washing before eating. But the washing after eating is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list of camp leniencies, the exemption from washing hands. אביי narrows it: the exemption covers only the washing before the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words sound like a blanket exemption from all hand-washing. אביי splits hand-washing into two kinds. The washing before the meal (מים ראשונים) is waived in the camp. The washing after the meal (מים אחרונים) stays a full obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual washing of the hands
'They only taught…', a formula that limits a source to a narrower case
'First waters': washing hands before eating bread
'Final waters': washing hands after the meal, before ברכת המזון
An obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as freeing soldiers from every kind of hand-washing. According to אביי, only the washing before the meal is waived.

phrases.english: And they are exempt from washing hands.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה's list of things made easier for soldiers in an army camp.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מַיִם רִאשׁוֹנִים,
phrases.english: Abaye said: They taught this only about first waters,
but final waters are an obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the burial topic (מת מצוה) to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The camp exemption covers only מים ראשונים. מים אחרונים remain obligatory.

steps.title: Why washing after the meal is required: dangerous salt
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי explains the reason for מים אחרונים: there is מלח סדומית, which can blind the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said: Why did the חכמים say that washing after the meal is required? Because there is salt from סדום, which blinds the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אשי asks his own question and answers it. He explains why washing after the meal is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for מים אחרונים is safety, not ritual purity. Salt from סדום might stay on the fingers and blind a person who touches his eyes. Soldiers are not exempt from protecting their health, so this washing stays required even in the camp.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason?
Salt from the region of סדום, which is dangerous
Blinds

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains אביי's split in step 5. Washing before the meal can be waived in the camp, but washing after the meal is about danger, and danger is not waived.

phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ashi said:
For what reason did they say
that final waters are an obligation?
Because there is Sodomite salt,
which blinds the eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind אביי's ruling that מים אחרונים are a חובה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מים אחרונים are required because of the danger of מלח סדומית.

steps.title: How rare the dangerous salt is
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that מלח סדומית is found like one grain in an entire כור of salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And it is found like one grain in a whole כור of salt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a detail about the dangerous salt. It is very rare, about one grain mixed into a huge amount of regular salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that such a rare danger can be ignored. אביי's point is that even this tiny amount is enough to require washing. You cannot check every grain, so everyone must wash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is found
A tiny grain
A very large measure of volume

phrases.english: Abaye said: And it is found like a grain in a kor.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: קורטא (grain) and כורא (kor) sound alike

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail about the danger described in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלח סדומית is rare, about one grain per כור, yet the concern still applies.

steps.title: Must someone who measured salt wash his hands?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether someone who measured salt, outside of a meal, must wash his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: If someone measured salt, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about touching salt when no meal is involved. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we learned about washing after eating. The question is whether the danger rule also applies to a person who simply handled salt, for example while measuring it for sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Measures
Salt
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
One who measured salt, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the salt danger to a case with no meal
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does handling salt outside a meal require washing hands?

steps.title: Of course he must wash
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that this does not even need to be asked. He certainly must wash.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That does not need to be asked.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 8. Someone who handled salt surely must wash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger comes from the salt itself, not from the meal. A person who measured salt touched much more salt than someone who just ate. So the obligation is even more obvious for him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not even a question; it is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: Washing after the meal is required even in a military camp because of the danger of מלח סדומית. This applies all the more to anyone who handles salt.

phrases.english: He said to him: This need not be asked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Obviously he must wash, since the danger is in the salt itself.

steps.title: Source for feeding soldiers דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next exemption, דמאי, and supports it with a משנה that the poor and quartered soldiers may be fed דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the camp is exempt from דמאי. As we learned in a משנה: We may feed the poor דמאי, and we may feed quartered soldiers דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list, the exemption from דמאי. It shows a source that soldiers may eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמאי is produce bought from an עם הארץ, who might not have separated מעשרות. Normally one must separate them before eating. The other משנה lets us feed such produce to the poor and to soldiers (אכסניא), which supports the camp leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce that may not have been tithed, bought from an עם הארץ
We may feed (others)
Soldiers quartered among the population

steps.confusionAlert: Remember that דמאי is only produce whose tithes are in doubt. It is not produce known to be untithed (טבל), which stays forbidden.

phrases.english: And from demai.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the next part of the משנה.

phrases.english: As we learned: One may feed the poor demai,
and quartered soldiers demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause in the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting the poor and אכסניא to be fed דמאי

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about feeding דמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes a ברייתא. בית שמאי forbid feeding the poor and soldiers דמאי, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It was taught in a ברייתא. בית שמאי say: We may not feed the poor דמאי or quartered soldiers דמאי. בית הלל say: We may feed the poor דמאי and quartered soldiers דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shows that the rule from step 10 is really a dispute. The permission follows בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 10 sounded like an accepted rule. The ברייתא shows that בית שמאי disagree and require tithing even for the poor and soldiers. The permission, and with it the camp leniency, follows בית הלל, whose view is the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
The school of הלל

steps.whyThisMatters: It tells us the camp's leniency for דמאי follows בית הלל, and בית הלל's rulings are the accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: It was taught:
Beit Shammai say:
One may not feed the poor demai,
nor quartered soldiers demai.
And Beit Hillel say:
One may feed the poor demai,
and quartered soldiers demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the משנה quoted in step 10 follows בית הלל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feeding the poor and אכסניא דמאי is a dispute. בית שמאי forbid it and בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: The camp exemption covers only עירובי חצירות
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's exemption "ומלערב", דבי רבי ינאי limit it to עירובי חצירות. Soldiers must still make עירובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said soldiers are exempt from making an עירוב. The students of רבי ינאי said: this applies only to the עירוב for courtyards. For an עירוב of שבת boundaries, they are still obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next exemption in the משנה, the one from making an עירוב. דבי רבי ינאי explain which kind of עירוב the exemption covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of עירוב. עירובי חצירות allows carrying between courtyards and is only דרבנן, so the camp exemption applies to it. עירובי תחומין lets a person walk past the שבת boundary, and here soldiers get no exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: And from making an עירוב (the words quoted from the משנה)
The students (school) of רבי ינאי
An עירוב that joins courtyards so people may carry between them
An עירוב that extends the Shabbos walking boundary
They only taught this about (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: "And from making an eiruv" (quoting the Mishnah).
phrases.notes: The משנה lists this as one of the things soldiers in a camp are exempt from.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
They taught this only about courtyard eiruvin,
but for boundary eiruvin, they are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִלְּעָרֵב. אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the דמאי exemption (steps 10-11) to the next exemption in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The camp exemption from עירוב applies only to עירובי חצירות. Soldiers must still make עירובי תחומין.

steps.title: Support: boundary violations carry Torah-level lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's ברייתא says a person gets מלקות מדאורייתא for violating תחומין. So no leniency is given even in a camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: a person receives lashes by Torah law for breaking the rules of תחומין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain why soldiers are not exempt from עירובי תחומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תחומין is a Torah prohibition punished with מלקות, it is too serious to be waived for soldiers. Courtyard עירוב, by contrast, is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: As (he) taught in a ברייתא
They receive lashes (מלקות)
By Torah law (מדאורייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The lashes are not for failing to make an עירוב. They are for walking past the boundary without one.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiya taught:
One receives lashes for (violating) Shabbos boundaries
phrases.notes: The source is "אל יצא איש ממקומו ביום השביעי" (שמות 16:29).

phrases.english: by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason behind דבי רבי ינאי's distinction.
steps.raayaObject: Soldiers are obligated in עירובי תחומין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא: מלקות מדאורייתא for תחומין.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: no lashes for a prohibition written with אל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן challenges רבי חייא. The תחומין verse uses "אל" rather than "לא". Can such a לאו carry מלקות?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן objected: Do we give lashes for a prohibition worded with "אל"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן attacks רבי חייא's claim that one gets lashes for תחומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says "אל יצא איש". רבי יונתן seems to assume that a prohibition phrased with "אל" is weaker than one phrased with "לא", and so carries no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
A Torah negative commandment
Which is worded with the word "אל" (do not)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan strongly objected to it:
Do we give lashes for a prohibition worded with "al"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא brought as support in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling of מלקות for תחומין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse uses "אל", which (apparently) does not produce מלקות.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: אל also appears by אוב and ידעוני
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב challenges רבי יונתן's objection. The איסור of אוב and ידעוני also uses "אל", and there one surely gets מלקות. This forces the גמרא to reinterpret רבי יונתן in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objected: If so, the verse says "Do not (אל) turn to the אוב and ידעוני." Would you say there too that one does not get lashes?!
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא attacks רבי יונתן's objection by pointing to a verse where "אל" clearly does lead to מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אל" cannot be what stops מלקות, since the לאו of אוב וידעוני also uses "אל" and does carry lashes. This sets up the גמרא's need to reinterpret רבי יונתן.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (pointing to an absurd result)
Forms of necromancy and sorcery forbidden by the Torah
So too? (Would you really say this?)

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov objected:
But if so, regarding what is written:
"Do not turn to the ov and the yidoni" (Vayikra 19:31),
would you say there too that one does not get lashes?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning behind רבי יונתן's objection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the wording "אל" prevents מלקות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: "אל" appears in the לאו of אוב וידעוני, which does carry lashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's objection, read as claiming that a לאו worded with "אל" carries no מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לאו of אוב וידעוני ("אל תפנו") is also worded with "אל" and does carry מלקות, so the word "אל" cannot be what blocks lashes.

steps.title: רבי יונתן's real difficulty: a prohibition tied to capital punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רבי יונתן. His problem is not the word "אל". The verse is a לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת בית דין, and no מלקות is given for such a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what bothered רבי יונתן: it is a prohibition given as a warning for a court-imposed death penalty. Any such prohibition does not receive lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יונתן really meant, so his objection to רבי חייא still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse "אל יצא איש ממקומו" is also the source for הוצאה (carrying out), which carries סקילה. Since this לאו serves as the warning for a death penalty, the rule is that it never carries מלקות, even in the תחומין case where no death penalty applies.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was difficult for him

keyTerms.term: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין
keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition given as the warning for a court death penalty
No lashes are given for it

steps.whatToRemember: There are no lashes for a לאו whose main role is to warn about a בית דין death penalty. רבי יונתן therefore disputes רבי חייא for this reason, not because of the word "אל".
steps.confusionAlert: Walking past the תחום is not itself a capital crime. The point is that the same verse also warns about a capital crime (הוצאה), and that is what blocks the lashes.

phrases.english: This is what was difficult for Rabbi Yonatan:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: It is a prohibition given as a warning for court-imposed death.
phrases.notes: The same verse is the source for the prohibition of carrying out, which carries סקילה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין —
phrases.english: And any prohibition given as a warning for court-imposed death —
one does not get lashes for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא בר יעקב by restating רבי יונתן's objection on new grounds.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יונתן objected because of the word "אל".
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יונתן objected because the לאו serves as the warning for מיתת בית דין, so it carries no מלקות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It brings in the general rule of לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת בית דין. That rule now stands against רבי חייא's ruling of מלקות for תחומין.

steps.title: The verse says 'go out,' not 'carry out'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the idea that "אל יצא איש ממקומו" is the warning for carrying on שבת. The verse only speaks about a person going out, which is the law of תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Is it written "do not carry out"? It is written "do not go out"!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back against Step 16's claim that the תחומין verse is also the warning for the death-penalty sin of carrying (הוצאה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the verse cannot give מלקות because it also serves as the warning for a sin punished by מיתת בית דין. רב אשי notes that the verse uses the word for walking out, not for carrying out. So it is only about תחומין, which carries no death penalty, and the objection to רבי חייא's ruling of מלקות falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: "Do not carry out": the wording that would refer to carrying objects (הוצאה)
"Do not go out": the actual wording of the verse, about a person walking
Carrying from one domain to another on שבת, punished by סקילה
"Is it written...?": a formula that rejects a reading by checking the exact words of the verse

steps.confusionAlert: Only one letter separates יוֹצִיא (carry out) from יֵצֵא (go out). The whole argument depends on that difference. The verse is about the person moving, not about objects being moved.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once the verse is limited to walking, תחומין is an ordinary לאו with no death penalty attached. That supports רבי חייא's ruling from Step 13 that one gets מלקות for violating תחומין.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Is it written "No man shall carry out"?
phrases.notes: This is the wording that would be needed for the verse to warn against carrying.

phrases.english: "No man shall go out" is written.
phrases.notes: So the verse only covers going out past the תחום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 16's premise that the תחומין verse also serves as the warning for the death-penalty sin of carrying.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that "אל יצא איש ממקומו" is a לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת בית דין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse says "go out," not "carry out," so it cannot be the source for the prohibition of הוצאה. It speaks only of תחומין, which carries no death penalty.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק מבוי
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line that ends the first פרק of עירובין, פרק מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, מבוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The first פרק of עירובין ends here, with the traditional promise to come back and learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the discussion of מבוי and its related topics is finished, and that a new פרק is about to start.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the formula said when finishing a perek
An alleyway; also the name of the first perek of עירובין

steps.whatToRemember: פרק מבוי ends with רב אשי's point that the תחומין verse is only about walking. Because of that, its לאו is not tied to מיתת בית דין.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "An Alleyway"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek that Step 17 finished.

steps.title: New פרק: boards may be set up around wells
steps.stepSummary: The משנה of the second פרק opens with the basic rule. One may set up פסין (upright boards) around a well.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may make boards for wells.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new פרק begins. Its first rule is that boards may be placed around a well in a public area so people can draw water on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A well is deep and wide enough to count as a רשות היחיד, but it sits in a public area. Drawing water from it and carrying it out would mean moving between domains. Surrounding the area with boards turns it into an enclosed private area, so drawing and using the water there is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: "Our משנה": marks the start of a new משנה
Upright boards or posts used to form a partition
Wells

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opening rule of the whole פרק. Everything that follows explains how these boards must be built and when they may be used.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may make upright boards
for wells.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new perek and a new topic, unrelated to the previous argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boards (פסין) may be set up around a well to allow drawing water on שבת.

steps.title: How many boards: רבי יהודה versus רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says four corner pieces are enough, and they look like eight boards. רבי מאיר requires eight pieces that look like twelve: four corner pieces plus four flat boards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four corner pieces that look like eight boards, says רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: eight that look like twelve, meaning four corner pieces and four plain boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a מחלוקת about how many boards are needed around the well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דיומד is a corner piece made of two boards joined at a right angle, so it looks like two boards. For רבי יהודה, four corners alone are enough, which looks like eight boards. רבי מאיר adds one plain flat board between each pair of corners, giving eight pieces that look like twelve boards.

keyTerms.meaning: Corner pieces made of two boards joined at a right angle
Plain, flat single boards
"Look like": how the pieces appear when counted

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "look like eight" does not mean eight separate pieces. It means four corner pieces, each of which looks like two boards.

phrases.english: Four double corner-posts
that look like eight,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says:
eight that look like twelve:
four double corner-posts
and four plain boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעָה דְּיוֹמְדִין נִרְאִין כִּשְׁמוֹנָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the boards from Step 19 must be arranged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires four corner pieces. רבי מאיר requires four corner pieces plus four plain boards.

steps.title: The size of each board
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the size of each board around the well: ten טפחים high, six טפחים wide, and any thickness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their height is ten handbreadths, their width is six, and their thickness can be any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us how big each board must be. It must be tall enough, wide enough, and thick enough to count as a valid board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten טפחים is the standard height for a מחיצה in the laws of שבת. A board shorter than that does not count as a wall. The width of six טפחים gives each board enough size to look like a real section of wall. Thickness does not matter at all, so even a very thin board works.

keyTerms.meaning: Handbreadths, a unit of measure (about 8-10 cm each)
Height
Width
Thickness
Any amount at all, even the smallest

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the size of each board with the gap between boards. This step is only about the board itself. The gap comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Their height is ten handbreadths,
phrases.notes: The standard minimum height for a halachic wall

phrases.english: and their width is six,
phrases.notes: Six טפחים, which is one אמה

phrases.english: and their thickness is any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by giving the size of the boards whose number was just debated
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each board must be 10 טפחים high and 6 טפחים wide. Any thickness is fine.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's maximum gap between the boards
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the space between the boards may be as wide as two teams of three cows each.
steps.simpleTranslation: And between them may be the space of two teams of three cattle each. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now sets how far apart the boards may stand. רבי מאיר gives the measure using teams of cows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for these boards is to let the animals of pilgrims drink. So the gap is measured by animal teams: two teams of three cows each, standing side by side. The גמרא will later work out this measure in אמות. The gaps here are much bigger than normal wall gaps, which is a special leniency for wells.

keyTerms.meaning: Teams of cattle (animals harnessed or grouped together)
Cattle, cows or oxen
As much as the full space of

steps.whyThisMatters: Normally a gap of more than ten אמות breaks a wall. Here a much larger gap is allowed, which shows how special the leniency of פסי ביראות is.

phrases.english: And between them
phrases.notes: The gap between one board and the next

phrases.english: may be the full space of two teams
of three cattle each,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the size of each board, the משנה gives the largest gap allowed between boards
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the gap between boards may equal the width of two teams of three cows each.

steps.title: רבי יהודה allows a slightly bigger gap
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the gap may be the width of two teams of four cows each. The cows are tied together, with one team entering and one leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: two teams of four cows each, tied together and not loose, one team going in and one coming out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר and allows a slightly larger gap. He also explains exactly how the cows are counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses teams of four cows instead of three, so his gap is a bit wider. He adds two conditions. The cows must be tied close together, not spread out loosely. The space is measured as one team entering while the other leaves. This keeps the measure from growing too large.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied together, kept tight in a group
Untied, loose, spread apart
Entering
Leaving, going out

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוּתָּרוֹת does NOT mean "permitted." It means "untied" or "loose." The same root appears in the next step with its usual meaning, "it is permitted."

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
teams of four,
phrases.notes: Four cows per team instead of three

phrases.english: tied and not untied,
phrases.notes: The cows are measured tightly grouped

phrases.english: one entering and one leaving.
phrases.notes: The two teams pass each other in the gap

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing measure to רבי מאיר's gap
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the gap may equal two teams of four tied cows, one entering and one leaving.

steps.title: Placing the boards close to the well
steps.stepSummary: The boards may be set close to the well, as long as a cow's head and most of its body fit inside while it drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted to bring the boards close to the well, as long as a cow can have its head and most of its body inside while drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the smallest allowed enclosure. The boards may be close to the well, but there must still be room for a cow to drink from inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this gave the largest gap allowed. This step gives the closest the boards may stand to the well. The minimum is set by the purpose of the boards, which is watering animals. A cow must be able to stand with its head and most of its body inside the enclosure while it drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring close
Well
Provided that, on condition that
Its head and the majority of its body

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole leniency of פסי ביראות exists so animals can drink. That is why both the largest gap and the smallest enclosure are measured by cows.

phrases.english: It is permitted to bring them close to the well,
phrases.notes: The boards may stand near the well

phrases.english: provided that a cow
has its head and most of its body inside
phrases.notes: Inside the enclosed area

phrases.english: and drinks.
phrases.notes: Measured while the cow is drinking

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the largest gap between boards to the closest the boards may stand to the well
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boards may be close to the well, as long as a cow's head and most of its body fit inside while it drinks.

steps.title: Opening word of the next rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins its next rule with the word "permitted." The rest of the rule appears on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the first word of the next rule in the משנה. The משנה is setting up its next rule, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule just before this was about bringing the boards close to the well. The parallel wording suggests the next rule will deal with moving the boards farther away. We should wait for the full sentence before drawing any conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted

phrases.english: It is permitted
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the next clause of the משנה, parallel to the previous rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. The ruling continues on the next amud.
